operations.hypothesis: Repairing a text-serialised native tool call into exactly one real tool call (when its click value is clickable) recovers the turn lost in case 300, and suppressing 'buy now' when instruction-matching clickable labels are still unclicked or the lowest displayed price exceeds the instruction ceiling (goal_cap from h5_purchase_skill, gate_block from h4_page_monitor) prevents the terminal wrong purchases seen in 961, 806 and 300 without touching the successful flows in 674, 488, 417, 885, 720 and 684.

Re-deriving the product-page verdict before every solver turn and publishing it in shared state (gate_block) gives the same-turn H2 guard a reliable channel, warns the solver one turn earlier in the same words the guard will use, and reports a click value that was not clickable on the page it was issued against (case 465).

A cold-start purchase procedure (search wording, title comparison against every requirement, read 'Price:' before buying, click every instruction-matching option, never click section headings, one tool call per turn) plus the parsed price ceiling in shared state gives the solver the domain policy the scaffold does not supply.

Appending one sentence to the click_action description only (names, order and schemas untouched) restates the two observed click failures - clicking a section heading such as 'size', and buying before selecting instruction-matching options or above the stated price - at the point where the model chooses the value.

rounds.bundle_hypothesis: Most WebShop rollouts that fail after a correct product choice end in a terminal 'buy now' that the public page contradicts: an option label copied verbatim from the instruction ('2-pack', 'black & gold', 'sweet & spicy') is clickable but was never clicked, or the lowest displayed price is above the instruction ceiling. A shared monitored verdict (options pending / price above ceiling) plus an action-layer guard that suppresses exactly those terminal actions, a cold-start procedure and one description sentence should remove those failures while leaving the observed successful trajectories (option clicked before buying, no-option pages, price range whose minimum is inside the ceiling) bit-identical.
